Governor Kehoe Announces Six Gubernatorial Appointments

November 27, 2026

Jefferson City

Today, Governor Kehoe announced five gubernatorial appointments to various boards and commissions and filled one county vacancy.
Michael Daming
, of St. Louis, was appointed to the 
Truman State University Board of Governors.
Mr. Daming is an attorney with Wasinger, Daming, LC. He previously served as chairman of the City of Brentwood Planning and Zoning Commission. Daming holds a bachelor's degree in political science and english from Truman State University and a Juris Doctor from the University of Missouri-Columbia.
Keith Dietzschold
, of Boonville, was appointed to the 
State Fair Commission.
Mr. Dietzschold served as director of agricultural education and state FFA advisor with the Missouri Department of Elementary and Secondary Education before retiring earlier this year. He was a member of the National Association of Agricultural Educators and the Missouri Vocational Agriculture Teachers Association. Dietzschold holds a bachelor's degree in animal science and a master's degree in practical arts and vocational and technical education from the University of Missouri-Columbia.
Lesa Mason
, of Pilot Knob, was appointed as 
Iron County Public Administrator.
Ms. Mason served as a victim advocate for the Iron County Prosecutor's Office. Mason holds an Associate of Applied Science in Judicial Administration from Mineral Area College.
Michael Tsichlis
, of Fenton, was appointed to the 
Missouri Advisory Council on Historic Preservation.
Mr. Tsichlis is an independent writer, researcher, and historian. He also served on the Lindbergh School District Board of Education. Tsichlis holds a Bachelor of Arts in Political Science and Russian and East European studies, a Master of Arts in Public Administration, and a Ph.D. in Public Policy Analysis and Administration from Saint Louis University.
Lesley McDaniel
, of Jefferson City, was appointed to the 
Missouri Advisory Council on Historic Preservation.
Ms. McDaniel previously worked as an architectural historian with the Missouri State Historic Preservation Office before retiring in 2024. She is a member of Friends of the Missouri State Archives, the Historic City of Jefferson, and the Daughters of the American Revolution. McDaniel holds a Bachelor of Science in Historic Preservation, Archaeology, History, and Anthropology from Southeast Missouri State University.
Natalie Hawn
, of St. Joseph, was reappointed to the 
Missouri Military Preparedness and Enhancement Commission.
Ms. Hawn is the president and CEO of the St. Joseph Chamber of Commerce. She is a member of the U.S. Chamber of Commerce, the Missouri Chamber of Commerce and Industry, and the Association of Chamber of Commerce Executives. Hawn holds a Bachelor of Arts in Communications from Missouri Western State University.
